title: Alex Honnold on Human Performance (part 1) – Where's the Limit?

reader_summary.headline: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast. I'm Doss, and this is part one of a two-part series with Alex Honnold on the future of human performance. As a professional rock climber, Alex has redefined the limits of what is possible by free soloing, that is climbing with no ropes or safety gear.

key_points.text: As a professional rock climber, Alex has redefined the limits of what is possible by free soloing.
key_points.evidence_quote: As a professional rock climber, Alex has redefined the limits of what is possible by free soloing, that is climbing with no ropes or safety gear, a 2,000-foot granite rock face in Yosemite, known as Alcapitan, a feat that was documented in the award-winning film Free Solo.

key_points.text: Part two is a fireside chat recorded last year as part of our A16s the Innovation Summit.
key_points.evidence_quote: Part two is a fireside chat recorded last year as part of our A16s the Innovation Summit.

key_points.text: In it, General Partner Peter Levine and Alex talk about the risk, preparation, and fear around his free solo.
key_points.evidence_quote: In it, General Partner Peter Levine and Alex talk about the risk, preparation, and fear around his free solo.

key_points.text: In this episode, I sit down with Alex and Peter, who, at age 59, is still an avid ice climber.
